quick: 10 mg twice daily; usual 10-20 mg twice daily (max 30 mg twice daily)
Use with caution; no major adjustment
summary: Nicorandil is an anti-anginal vasodilator that combines ATP-sensitive potassium-channel activation with a nitrate-like action, dilating both coronary arteries and peripheral vessels to reduce preload and afterload. It is used for angina pectoris, usually as add-on or second-line therapy. A characteristic and important adverse effect is ulceration (oral, anal, gastrointestinal, skin, and other mucosae), which mandates discontinuation. It is not FDA-approved.
indications: Prevention and long-term treatment of angina pectoris (often add-on to beta-blockers and/or calcium channel blockers, or when these are contraindicated/not tolerated)

dosage.d: Start 10 mg twice daily; usual maintenance 10-20 mg twice daily
dosage.n: A lower starting dose (5 mg twice daily) may be used if headache-prone; maximum 30 mg twice daily

dosage.d: Start 5 mg twice daily, then titrate up
dosage.n: Headache is common at initiation and usually transient

admin: Take morning and evening, with or without food
Titrate gradually; a lower initial dose limits the common early headache
Stop the drug if ulceration of skin, mucosa, eye, or gastrointestinal tract develops
moa: Nicorandil has a dual mechanism: it opens ATP-sensitive potassium (K-ATP) channels in vascular smooth muscle, causing hyperpolarisation and arterial (including coronary) vasodilatation that reduces afterload; and it has a nitrate moiety that stimulates guanylate cyclase, increasing cGMP and causing venodilatation that reduces preload. The net effect lowers myocardial oxygen demand and improves coronary blood flow.

absolute: Left ventricular failure with low filling pressures / acute pulmonary oedema
Concomitant use of phosphodiesterase-5 inhibitors (sildenafil, tadalafil, vardenafil) or riociguat
monitor: Skin, mucosal, ocular, and gastrointestinal ulceration
Signs of bleeding from ulcers / perforation

preg: There are insufficient data on use in pregnancy. Avoid unless clearly necessary and no safer alternative exists.
lact: It is not known whether nicorandil is excreted in human milk. Breastfeeding is not recommended during treatment.
renal: No specific dose adjustment is generally required, but use with caution and monitor blood pressure in renal impairment.
hepatic: Use with caution in hepatic impairment as metabolism may be altered; titrate carefully and monitor blood pressure.

major: Phosphodiesterase-5 inhibitors (sildenafil, tadalafil, vardenafil) - severe hypotension (contraindicated)
minor: Drugs lowering serum potassium (interact with K-ATP channel effect)
interactions.food: May be taken with or without food
interactions.diagnostics: Monitor blood pressure; investigate any non-healing ulcer for a drug cause

serious: Oral, anal, genital, gastrointestinal, and skin/mucosal ulceration
Gastrointestinal ulcer perforation, fistula, or bleeding
emergency: Gastrointestinal perforation or major bleeding from ulcers

monitoring: Blood pressure, particularly at initiation and dose increases
Development of skin, mucosal, ocular, anal, or gastrointestinal ulcers - stop the drug
Symptoms of GI bleeding or perforation
counsel: Headache is common when starting but usually settles - do not stop abruptly without advice
Report any mouth, anal, genital, eye, or skin ulcers, or persistent abdominal pain - these can be caused by the drug
Do not use erectile-dysfunction medicines (sildenafil-type drugs) with nicorandil - dangerous blood pressure drop
Rise slowly from sitting/lying to avoid dizziness; avoid alcohol
Seek urgent care for severe abdominal pain, black stools, or vomiting blood
pk: Approximately 1 hour (no tolerance like classic nitrates)
Store below 25 C; protect from moisture
pearls: Dual mechanism: K-ATP channel opening plus a nitrate effect - dilates coronary arteries and reduces pre/afterload
Beware drug-induced ulceration (mouth, anus, GI tract, skin, eye) - discontinue, as it heals on stopping
Contraindicated with PDE-5 inhibitors and riociguat due to severe hypotension
missed: Take the missed dose as soon as remembered unless it is nearly time for the next dose, in which case skip it and resume the usual schedule. Do not double the dose.
overdose: Overdose causes peripheral vasodilatation with hypotension and reflex tachycardia. Management is supportive: lay the patient flat, give intravenous fluids and, if needed, vasopressors to restore blood pressure; cardiac monitoring is advised. There is no specific antidote.
